best_lineage.idea: Add pairwise interaction (product and sign) features plus log-transform of the skewed x3 to make XOR/quadrant-like hidden rules linearly separable, since the linear model currently only sees raw inputs and weights are small/uniform (underfitting).

The weak weight on x6 (f5) and the fact that the strongest features are the x1*x2 product and its sign suggest the hidden rule is primarily the x1*x2 quadrant/XOR with log(x3) as a secondary signal; drop the dead x1*x6 and x2*x6 product features and their signs, and instead add cross-interactions between log(x3) and x1/x2 (the skewed input may gate the interaction), exposing new linear structure t

@@ -18,8 +18,21 @@
     Every row must give the same number of features. The classifier is linear in the
     features (they are standardized and a bias is added), so nonlinear structure only

+    x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6 = row
+    # log of skewed positive input (guard against non-positive)
+    lx3 = math.log(max(x3, 1e-9))
+    # core linear terms (keep x6 as a weak raw input)
+    feats = [x1, x2, lx3, x6]
+    # x1*x2 product and its sign: strongest known signal
+    p12 = x1 * x2
+    feats.append(p12)
+    feats.append(1.0 if p12 > 0 else -1.0)
+    # cross terms with the skewed input: let log(x3) gate the interaction
+    feats.append(p12 * lx3)
+    feats.append(x1 * lx3)
+    feats.append(x2 * lx3)
+    # soft bin of log(x3) to allow a threshold effect
+    feats.append(math.tanh((lx3 - 0.5) / 0.5))
